title: 14.2 A 16nm 216kb, 188.4TOPS/W and 133.5TFLOPS/W Microscaling Multi-Mode Gain-Cell CIM Macro Edge-AI Devices
problem: CIM macros face tradeoffs: integer CIM achieves high energy efficiency but limited accuracy; floating-point CIM provides higher accuracy but reduced efficiency; emerging microscaling (MX) formats improve accuracy-efficiency but require novel multi-mode CIM supporting MX-INT-FP with: system-to-CIM transfer overhead, costly adder trees, and inefficient data flows across variable accumulation sizes.
motivation: Optimal AI data format is workload-dependent; edge AI requires flexible CIM supporting multiple precision modes without excessive energy/area overhead.
method: The design combines a 16-nanometer chip with 216 kilobytes of gain-cell memory that supports three formats: microscaling (a compact format), integer, and floating-point. It converts floating-point data to microscaling format inside the computation rather than beforehand, using a specialized unit that tracks signal variance to maintain accuracy. The adder tree—which sums partial results—is optimized for high-probability operations, reducing wasted work in common cases. The chip dynamically reconfigures how it accumulates results based on the precision needed at each step.
key_novelty: The core contribution is enabling a single CIM chip to support microscaling, integer, and floating-point formats by performing format conversion inside the computation and using a pattern-aware adder tree optimized for high-probability operations.
contributions: In-CIM format conversion eliminating system-to-CIM overhead
primary_theme: Multi-mode CIM macro supporting flexible precision formats for edge AI
